name: Surface and Mesh Extraction
text:
# Surface and Mesh Extraction

Also called: Gaussian Meshing, 3DGS Meshing

## Overview
This family comprises methods to extract explicit triangular meshes from trained [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) models. Standard 3DGS represents scenes as implicit volumetric primitives, lacking a native surface representation. These methods solve the problem of obtaining watertight, textured geometry for downstream applications like simulation, AR/VR, or editing. They differ from sibling methods like [Radiative and Tomographic Gaussians](4971-radiative-and-tomographic-gaussians.md) by focusing on geometric extraction rather than physical property rendering, and from [Domain-Specific Adaptations](5621-domain-specific-adaptations.md) by targeting general mesh generation rather than specific domain constraints like microscopy.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate on the output of a trained 3DGS model $\mathcal{G} = \{G_i\}_{i=1}^M$. Each primitive $G_i$ is defined by position $\mathbf{p}_i$, covariance $\mathbf{\Sigma}_i$, opacity $\alpha_i$, and color attributes [Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md). The core challenge is converting these anisotropic, volumetric kernels into a discrete surface representation. This requires either evaluating the implicit density field defined by the Gaussians, leveraging geometric cues (depth/normal) rendered from the splats, or modifying the splat distribution to align with an existing mesh. The rendering pipeline's geometric projection remains consistent: 3D Gaussians are transformed into ray space, and the projected 2D covariance $\mathbf{\hat{\Sigma}}_i$ is computed using the Jacobian $J$ of the affine approximation of the projection and the rotation part $W$ of the extrinsic matrix:
$$ \mathbf{\hat{\Sigma}}_i = J W \mathbf{\Sigma}_i W^T J^T $$
[Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md)

## Subtopics

### [Gaussian Opacity Fields (GOF) Mesh Extraction](3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md)
A method to extract a 3-D triangulated mesh from a trained Gaussian model without retraining, by building a volumetric density field and extracting an isosurface [3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md]. It builds on [Surface and Mesh Extraction](8498-surface-and-mesh-extraction.md) by treating the Gaussian opacity field as a continuous volumetric density function, distinct from sibling methods that rely on distance fields or direct point-cloud reconstruction.

### [Distance-based Gaussian Splatting](7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md)
[Distance-based Gaussian Splatting](#7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md) is a method that integrates a pre-existing 3D mesh with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) primitives to improve rendering quality and geometric consistency in large-scale scenes. It solves the problem of redundant or distorted Gaussian splats in regions where the underlying mesh is inaccurate or overly dense by classifying splats as "tightly-bound" or "loosely-bound" based on their distance to the mesh surface. Unlike standard 3DGS which treats all primitives equally, this method masks occluded splats, prunes those hidden behind the mesh, and aligns tightly-bound splats to the mesh geometry, thereby reducing memory usage and preventing artifacts from mesh reconstruction errors [7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md].

### [2D-Lift-3D Scene Segmentation](11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md)
This method segments 3D Gaussian primitives by lifting 2D segmentation masks, generated from a reference view using foundation models like SAM, into 3D space via multi-view label voting [11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md]. It enables partial [scene editing](#17595-scene-editing.md) (PSE) by decomposing a scene into distinct Gaussian groups, allowing independent manipulation of color, opacity, and lighting [11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md]. Unlike methods that require learnable feature vectors or extensive training for segmentation [11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md], this approach is training-free and relies on geometric projection and voting, though it may require iterative refinement for complex scenes [11513-2d-lift-3d-scene-segmentation.md].

### [Mesh Extraction via Poisson Reconstruction](12790-mesh-extraction-via-poisson-reconstruction.md)
This method extracts a textured triangular mesh from an optimized 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) scene by converting rendered 2D depth and normal maps into a 3D oriented point cloud, which is then processed by a Poisson surface reconstruction algorithm [12790-mesh-extraction-via-poisson-reconstruction.md][12790-mesh-extraction-via-poisson-reconstruction.md]. It differs from direct meshing approaches like [Gaussian Opacity Fields (GOF)](#5992-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof.md) [3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md] or distance-based methods [7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md] by relying on post-processing rendered geometric cues rather than modifying the core [Gaussian representation](#5918-gaussian-based-representation.md) or optimizing a signed distance field [12790-mesh-extraction-via-poisson-reconstruction.md][12790-mesh-extraction-via-poisson-reconstruction.md].

## Background
The extraction of meshes from 3DGS is a necessary step for integrating [neural radiance fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) and Gaussian splats into traditional computer graphics pipelines. Early 3DGS implementations focused solely on novel view synthesis [Radiative Gaussian Splatting](3040-radiative-gaussian-splatting.md). Subsequent research identified the lack of explicit geometry as a limitation for applications requiring collision detection or texture mapping. Methods like GOF [3692-gaussian-opacity-fields-gof-mesh-extraction.md] and Poisson-based extraction [12790-mesh-extraction-via-poisson-reconstruction.md] emerged to bridge this gap, while distance-based approaches [7411-distance-based-gaussian-splatting.md] addressed geometric consistency in large-scale scenes.
